title: Odile and the Machine
premise: Edmund Reyes keeps the Meridian's long-range beacon running and avoids the cryo hold where two hundred backup copies of colonists sleep—copies made without consent, including one of the woman he loved, Odile Voss, who died on a survey mission years ago. When the research vessel Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward into childhood, Edmund discovers the beacon has been broadcasting an unlicensed signal that rewrites cellular time, and Odile's backup is the only mind old enough to decode it. To stop the signal from reaching the colony fleet, he must wake her copy—an act of inheritance and betrayal—and together they trace the signal to its source: his own dead mentor's hidden experiment. In the end, Edmund sacrifices his navigator's career and his clean conscience, choosing to let half the sleepers wake as children while Odile's copy, restored but changed, chooses to remember him even though he was never hers.
about_author: A. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote transmission stations in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about machines that outlive their makers, and live quietly with a partner and an aging shortwave receiver.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Edmund Reyes, POV. During a routine maintenance shift, Edmund repairs the Meridian's ancient beacon while avoiding the cryo hold below. He recites the names of the sleeping backups like a penance. Emotional beat: quiet guilt established; the reader learns he helped commission the backup program and has never forgiven himself.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Sleepers
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. A supply officer asks why the backups exist at all; Edmund deflects, then privately visits the hold and pauses at pod 114—Odile Voss. Flashback fragments of her death on the Kestrel survey. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into avoidance; he cannot decide if keeping her backup is love or cowardice.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The long-lost ship Halcyon appears on scope, broadcasting a distress call in a child's voice. Docking crews find thirty crew members biologically aged backward—adults' minds trapped in young bodies, memories intact. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as medical teams fail to reverse it.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Captain
chapters.summary: Captain Ilsa Moreau (aged eleven), POV. Moreau struggles to command her own ship from a child's body while officers pity her. She describes the deep-space anomaly they encountered: a region where 'time flowed wrong.' Emotional beat: dignity under humiliation; she insists the anomaly was artificial.

chapters.title: Pod 114
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Command orders all backups scanned for immunity data; Edmund realizes Odile's copy may hold the key—the backup process predates the anomaly and shares signal architecture with the beacon. Emotional beat: the choice he dreaded arrives dressed as duty; he signs the wake authorization with shaking hands.

chapters.title: Waking Is a Kind of Drowning
chapters.summary: Odile (the copy), POV. She wakes four years after her original's death, inheriting memories that end mid-sentence. She meets Edmund, who loved a woman she technically is but has never been. Emotional beat: disorientation and sharp humor; she refuses to be anyone's monument.

chapters.title: What the Backup Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Reviewing her own archived neural map, Odile finds embedded signal patterns matching the Halcyon's condition—proof the backup tech and the anomaly share an origin. Emotional beat: intellectual exhilaration shadowed by violation; someone used her death as infrastructure.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Following encrypted records, Edmund uncovers that Dr. Anselm Reyes—his mentor, possibly kin—designed both the beacon and the backup system as one experiment in 'reversible time.' Emotional beat: betrayal compounding guilt; the machine he maintained was always aimed at the sleepers.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Moreau, POV. The de-aged crew begins forming bonds among themselves, a strange new society of old minds in young bodies. Moreau warns command that the anomaly region is expanding toward the colony lane. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness; the afflicted refuse to be treated as casualties.

chapters.title: Duty Calls Him by Name
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Fleet command orders the beacon shut down—but shutdown will strand the Halcyon's crew in their condition permanently, since the signal also stabilizes them. Edmund must choose between the colony fleet's safety and thirty lives. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; duty and mercy point opposite ways.

chapters.title: Odile Argues With Her Ghost
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile confronts the memory archive of her original self, reading letters the dying woman left for 'whoever wakes.' The letter forgives Edmund but asks her copy to live for herself, not as a replacement. Emotional beat: mourning and self-authorization; she claims her own name.

chapters.title: The Signal's Heart
chapters.summary: Edmund and Odile, alternating. Tracing the beacon's core, they find Anselm's hidden laboratory module still orbiting in the debris field—a machine that can aim, amplify, or erase the time-signal. Emotional beat: partnership kindling between two people grieving the same woman from different sides.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Command council scene, ensemble POV. The mathematics are brutal: the signal can restore the Halcyon crew OR shield the two hundred sleepers from its spreading field—not both. Power allocation becomes a vote on whose future counts. Emotional beat: institutional coldness; Edmund watches colleagues reduce people to line items.

chapters.title: Ages Backward
chapters.summary: Moreau, POV. The field reaches the Meridian's outer ring; a young technician de-ages overnight. Panic spreads through the crew. Moreau, now the station's foremost expert on the condition, must teach others how to survive it. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into leadership; the afflicted become the guides.

chapters.title: What Edmund Buried
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Full flashback: years ago, Edmund signed off on the backup program believing it was archival only, then falsified logs when he learned Anselm intended to use the sleepers as test subjects. His guilt kept the beacon running ever since. Emotional beat: confession to Odile; the truth costs him command's trust.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Working around the clock, Odile finds Anselm's unfinished protocol: a phased pulse that could age the Halcyon crew forward gradually while damping the field's spread—if someone pilots a relay drone into the anomaly itself. One-way trip. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; she volunteers before Edmund can.

chapters.title: Vote of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Command puts the plan to the affected parties: the de-aged crew votes to risk the pulse; the sleepers cannot vote, so Odile argues on their behalf—that waking into a shortened, altered life beats sleeping forever. Emotional beat: democracy as moral labor; the room chooses courage twice.

chapters.title: Launch Window
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund insists on flying the relay himself—he built the beacon, he knows its language. He and Odile spend the pre-launch hours not confessing love but building it, ordinary and unhurried. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved not by sacrifice alone but by claiming joy first.

chapters.title: Into the Wrong Time
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Inside the anomaly, time stutters—Edmund experiences his own past and possible futures overlapping as he aligns the relay. The pulse fires. The field collapses inward. Emotional beat: sublime terror; he navigates by memory of Odile's voice rather than instruments.

chapters.title: Growing Forward
chapters.summary: Moreau, POV. Across the Meridian, the de-aged crew ages back over days—restored, scarred, carrying new tenderness for each other. The sleepers' pods stabilize, safe but still sleeping; the fleet will decide their waking later, properly this time. Emotional beat: relief braided with loss; some things cannot be fully repaired.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Edmund and Odile, alternating. Edmund, stripped of rank for his old falsifications, accepts demotion to civilian beacon-keeper. The colony votes to wake the backups voluntarily, each given the choice Odile had. Emotional beat: accountability without despair; institutions bend because individuals refused to let them break people.

chapters.title: The Keeper and the Copy
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Final chapter: Odile, choosing to stay rather than seek her original's old life, joins Edmund at the beacon. Together they rewrite the backup charter—no copies without consent, no sleepers without a say. The last image: two lights, the beacon above and the hold below, both tended. Emotional beat: resolution as ongoing choice; love and memory inherited deliberately, not by accident.
